candidates.finding: Determine whether explicit shared-tree child isolation evades same-turn writable-task worktree stamping in first-party Agent dispatch.
candidates.screening_result: Original MIT main@ed4b4be equals reviewed ref, no open upstream PRs. Agent.run stamps each of two+ writable task calls with isolation=worktree unless already worktree; input.isolation=none is NOT taskWantsWorktree and is overwritten. spawnChild only permits the configured isolated worktree path, and first-party native test asserts two writable calls are auto-isolated. Hypothesized explicit-none shared checkout escape falsified in code; no new patch/native test run or universal concurrency guarantee.

candidates.finding: Determine whether supported symlink aliases to one real git worktree permit concurrent duplicate sdd-remediate worker admission.
candidates.screening_result: Original MIT current main@74c40493 (drift from Index reviewed 40740437) uses canonicalWriterRoot resolving realpath/Git root for bounded writable worker claims. Runner atomically checks and reserves WriterSurfaceRegistry per canonical root; native first-party test asserts symlinked cwd and real root share a key and conflict, independent worktrees do not. Predicted symlink spelling escape is contradicted by shipped code/tests; no new external patch or test run.

candidates.finding: Determine whether parent-directory and nested-file declared expected_write_scope values fail first-party sibling collision detection.
candidates.screening_result: Original MIT main@32542e9 differs substantially from Index review_ref 2319ec3. At reviewed ref, writeScopesOverlap compares both file and directory PathPrefix via normalizedScopeAbsPath/pathWithinScope (so parent/nested prefix is already detected). Current registry instead classifies explicit task identity/semantic probable duplicates, with no expected_write_scope/WriteScope predicate in current registry or tool. Old scope hypothesis is already false on reviewed source and no longer applicable to current source; no native change justified and no Index grade re-evaluation asserted.

candidates.finding: Determine whether cancellation of one active first-party queued Approve request permanently blocks another waiting sibling child from receiving its approval.
candidates.screening_result: Original MIT main@430a830 differs from Index reviewed 9fafafb, no open upstream PR. queuedApprover.Approve takes PromptSlotFor(ctx) and defers slot.Release immediately after successful Acquire; cancellation while queued returns ctx.Err. Native first-party tests specifically assert queued cancellation, waiter count decrement and next waiter progress after release. Predicted permanent slot-hold on cancel not supported; no additional patch/native runner invoked.
